subject: Risk & Compliance
title: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act
description: A 60-second lesson on The Sarbanes-Oxley Act.

hook.text: After Enron and WorldCom collapsed, Congress passed the strictest corporate governance law in US history.

buildup.text: Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) requires CEOs to personally certify financial statements and strengthens internal controls.

discovery.text: SOX created the PCAOB to oversee auditors and made destroying financial records a federal crime.

twist.text: Compliance costs billions annually. Small companies argue SOX is too expensive for their scale.

climax.text: SOX restored investor confidence but showed that governance reforms only come after catastrophic fraud.

punchline.text: Enron fell. SOX rose. CEOs now sign the numbers.

quiz.question: What does SOX require CEOs to do?
options: Personally certify the accuracy of financial statements
